newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says it takes no sides in Zaire conflict.
newsitem.headline: France says it takes no sides in Zaire conflict.

text.p: France, distancing itself from embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko, said on Wednesday it was not taking sides in the conflict between Zaire's government and rebels and it was up to the Zairean people to decide their fate.
"We are not supporting anyone. What we support is Zaire and the future of its people," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a news briefing.
"France does not recognise governments. It recognises states," he added.
Rummelhardt's statement was the strongest sign to date that France was keeping its distance from Mobutu, who has enjoyed Paris's support throughout most of his 32-year autocratic rule.
Rummelhardt said Tuesday's agreement by the warring sides in South Africa on the need for a ceasefire was a step in the right direction but stressed the need for a time frame for its implementation.
"The statement published yesterday contains very positive elements but we must regret that no date has been set for the implementation of the ceasefire," Rummelhardt said.
Rebel forces led by Laurent Kabila have seized about a third of Zaire, including major mining areas, as Mobutu's ragged troops flee or even switch sides,
